name: Example App
description: One sentence on what this project IS, then a sentence starting 'Improved by learnings about ...' naming the subjects that genuinely change it. The second sentence matters most: name + description + keywords are what get embedded, so the vocabulary here decides which learnings are ever offered to the judge. Describe the project in the words a relevant learning would itself use — 'agent memory, tool-use reliability, MCP servers' finds far more than 'TypeScript/Express bot'.
keywords: terms a relevant learning would actually contain
avoid: the near-miss category this project keeps attracting. Only the judge sees this, never the embedding — so it can raise precision but can never recover a learning the prefilter already dropped. Name what is adjacent-but-wrong; do not exclude the project's own subject, or it will reject the learnings you most want.

name: Example CLI
description: A command-line tool for X. Improved by learnings about the specific mechanics it implements. Projects without a path get chips and find_for_project results but no IDEAS.md drops.
